E2 demonstrates synthesis of graphene shell-encapsulated HEA nanoparticles, but provides no evidence that the shell acts as an oxidation barrier or preserves composition under high-temperature oxidative conditions; this barrier function is assumed without direct support.
premises: Oxidation of equiatomic HEA nanoparticles is driven by atomic size and redox potential, with redox potential dominating over time and causing compositional inversion.
Graphene shells can be synthesized conformally on HEA nanoparticles via laser solid-phase synthesis on LIG supports.
A graphene shell acts as a physical barrier that limits oxygen access to the nanoparticle surface.
Preventing oxygen access inhibits the oxidation mechanism, thereby preserving near-equiatomic composition and structural integrity.
